class_reason: All six Table 1 targets (four PSPM coefficients and two vertex counts) reproduce to the printed rounding from the deposited code and data, and the pre-registered reduced bootstrap (authors' seeds 1..K, K = 4) keeps every T1-T4 coefficient positive with estimate - 1.96 x SD > 0 (batch4_class_decisions.md #3). Alternative class if only the full 120-draw bootstrap counts: E (about 19 CPU-hours, out of scope on this machine).
confidence_reason: Point estimates and counts match to the printed rounding and the four seed-1..4 draws per model equal the deposited bootstrap rows (max abs diff in outputs/boot_vs_deposited.csv, see other_checks), but significance rests on K = 4 draws instead of the paper's 120, several packages are newer than the authors' (igraph 2.1.4, reticulate 1.41.0.1, rgeos/rgdal removed), and B has not been compared yet.
env_fixes: diffs/analysis_globals_E1_E2_E3.diff: E1 RETICULATE_PYTHON to the run venv python (lines 58, 120); E2 ncore 40 -> 1 (line 46); E3 library(rgeos)/library(rgdal) removed (lines 69-70, 125-126) because rgeos 0.6-4 and rgdal 1.6-7 fail to build (sp.h missing; sp 2.x ships no headers). All pre-registered.

diffs/analysis_pool_A.diff: pre-registered run structure F1 (one model per process), F2 (lapply instead of parLapply, no cluster), F3 (save to outputs/, 120-draw bootstrap replaced by pre-registered step 6). Estimation code unchanged.

Package versions (no diff): pinned miscTools 0.6-26, maxLik 1.5-2, texreg 1.38.6, infotheo 1.2.0.1 used; pinned reticulate 1.28 built but cannot start Python >= 3.12 (config.py imports the removed 'imp' module), replaced by Debian reticulate 1.41.0.1; pinned igraph 1.4.1 fails to compile (-Werror=format-security), Debian igraph 2.1.4 used; cshapes 2.0 needed V8 built from CRAN source with DOWNLOAD_STATIC_LIBV8=1 (Debian r-cran-v8 conflicts with the preinstalled nodejs).
uncertainties: The printed 95% percentile brackets (120 draws) were not reproduced; significance for T1-T4 uses K = 4 draws with the authors' seeds 1-4 (estimate +/- 1.96 x SD), a much less precise interval than the paper's. With K = 4 the SD itself is very uncertain.

The machine restarted twice during the run (00:53 and 01:55 IST); every reported number comes from processes that completed after the first restart, with the same package versions before and after (checked). The second restart interrupted the robustness queue.

Memory: the brief's 3.5 GB MemAvailable threshold could not be met before the first restart (in-RAM root filesystem used about 4.8 GB); the first two (discarded or repeat) fits started at 2.3-2.4 GB. All reported runs after the first restart started with at least 3.5 GB available. Peak RSS per process was 1.43-1.47 GB.

Package versions differ from the authors' (R 4.5.0 aarch64 vs R 4.2.2 x86_64; igraph 2.1.4, reticulate 1.41.0.1, numpy 2.5.3, networkx 3.7, scipy 1.18.1). The exact agreement of the bootstrap draws with the deposited ones suggests this did not matter for these numbers.

Code review covered analysis_globals.R, analysis_pool.R, main_plots_tables.R lines 1-80, and in the pspm package R/fit_pspm.R (model_graphframe, fit_pspm_model) and R/pspm_R6.R (composite likelihood, fit, bootstrap, reset); the Python lattice code (sl3.py) was not reviewed line by line. No bug found. Unverified observation (design, not a bug): the Gaussian penalty sum(beta^2)/(2*sigma2) also applies to the Constant.

Not run (wall-time limit, about 2 hours, after the two restarts): R_b and R_c refits of the secondary pool_ldv model (T2 cuteth_lag), and R_a draws (seeds 1001-1004) for pool_ldv. R_a, R_b and R_c were run for the primary quantity T1 (pool_xsec) only. The pool_xsec R_a draws ran in a process that also refitted pool_xsec (outputs/fit_pool_xsec_ra.csv, identical to the main fit).

Reduced bootstrap: K = 4 draws per seed set (pre-registered rule K = min(10, floor(25/t)) with t = 5.19 min for the first draw; outputs/boot_K.json), not the paper's 120. R_b and R_c significance reuse the step-6 SD of the main model (PREREG section 3), they were not bootstrapped themselves.
R_a SD ratio (seeds 1001-1004 vs 1-4) is within a factor 1.5 for cuteth but exceeds it for length.norm and watershed_diff.norm (outputs/boot_sd_ratio.csv); with K = 4 the SD itself is very imprecise.

R_b changed the counts (pool_xsec vertices 6769 to 6739, edges 17923 to 17193, states 189 to 220, outputs/counts_pool_xsec_rb.csv) and several control coefficients moved substantially (for example elevmean.norm, outputs/fit_pool_xsec_rb.csv); cuteth stayed positive and significant under the pre-registered rule.

The final scripts (extract_targets.R, boot_summary.R, environment.sh, build_results.py) were run at 02:35-02:43 IST by a continuation of agent A after the first agent A instance hit its iteration limit; no model was refitted in that step.
